heroHeadline: US FORMAL NATO WITHDRAWAL PLAN EXPECTED IN JUNE; RUSSIA DEFLECTS GALATI BLAME; NATO COUNTER-DRONE MEASURES ANNOUNCED; 'MILITARY SCHENGEN' EXPANSION PROPOSED — ANKARA SUMMIT 37 DAYS OUT
heroSubtitle: As of May 31, 2026, the NATO-US crisis enters a new phase of formalization: the United States is preparing to submit a comprehensive European force-level withdrawal plan to allied governments as early as June — the first formal NATO-wide documentation of a multi-domain US military drawdown in alliance history. The plan is expected to codify the 10,200+ confirmed troop reductions from Germany and Poland, plus the hardware contribution cuts secretly disclosed by Pentagon adviser Velez-Green on May 26 (Der Spiegel): fighter jets available to NATO cut by one-third, strategic bombers halved, zero US submarines contributed, zero US drones. European allies have been pressing for the formal document since Helsingborg (May 21–22) produced no withdrawal parameters; the June submission will give defense ministries approximately six weeks to develop national gap-filling plans before the Ankara Leaders' Summit (July 7–8). Meanwhile, Russia's diplomatic deflection of the Galati drone strike (May 28–29) continued on May 30, with Moscow's MFA claiming the Geran-2 that struck a NATO apartment building was 'likely Ukrainian' — a characterization NATO, Romania, and the US State Department rejected as a 'transparent disinformation operation.' Romania completed the closure of the Russian Consulate General in Constanta and expelled the Russian Consul-General. NATO announced it is working to bring Romania's MEROPS counter-drone network under direct NATO command and to expedite anti-drone capability transfers to Romanian forces — the alliance's first concrete operational response to the 28-strike pattern of drone incursions into Romanian airspace. Separately, proposals emerged May 31 to expand the Netherlands-Germany-Poland 'Military Schengen' free-movement-of-forces corridor to include France and the Baltic states — a structural European defense integration measure that would create a 3,500 km contiguous rapid-reinforcement arc from the Atlantic coast to the Russian border, compensating for the US drone and submarine contribution withdrawals.
